newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia announces stiff electricity rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia announces stiff electricity rate hike.

text.p: Stiff rate hikes for electricity will take effect in Colombia next year, and the country's richest homes will bear the brunt of the increase along with business and industry, Mines and Eenergy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said Tuesday.

Villamizar told reporters the increases, effective January 1, would be based on the government's official inflation target for 1997. That target has not been announced yet, but government sources quoted in recent press reports say it will be set at 18 percent.

According to Villamizar, the poorest homes in Colombia will be required to pay an electric rate hike equal to the inflation target plus two percentage points -- a 20 percent increase if the target is indeed set at 18 percent.
The country's wealthiest homes will pay a premium equal to 20 percentage points above the inflation target, however, as will businesses and industrial plants across Colombia, Villamizar said.

Stiff price hikes for electricity and other public services triggered riots in a working-class district on the outskirts of Bogota in September but the government says they are necessary as part of an effort to slash subsidies and get its fiscal house in order.
